payload.text:
I reviewed `share-editing` against `main` (3 commits, 8 files) and didn't change any code. All the tests pass, but there's one serious bug they don't catch, so **I wouldn't merge yet**.

**🔴 Blocker: anyone who can view a document can also edit it (`src/guard.js`, `canEdit`)**
```js
return share.mask & WRITE === WRITE && !share.locked;
```
JavaScript evaluates `===` before `&`, so this line actually runs as `share.mask & (WRITE === WRITE)`, which is `share.mask & 1`. That checks for READ, not WRITE. I ran it to confirm:
- `canEdit({ mask: READ, locked: false })` returns **`true`**, so a view-only link gets edit access.
- `canEdit({ mask: COMMENT | WRITE, locked: false })` returns **`0`**, so someone with WRITE but no READ can't edit.

The tests miss this because the only editor case they check also has READ. The fix is to use `hasRight(share.mask, WRITE) && !share.locked`, the same way `canComment` does. Please also add a test that a viewer can't edit.

**🟡 Smaller points in `src/ownership.js`, `transferOwnership`**
- **No ownership check:** it never confirms that `fromUser` is the current `doc.owner`. If callers don't check this first, anyone could hand ownership to anyone.
- **Giving ownership to yourself breaks it:** if `fromUser === toUser`, ADMIN is removed and then all rights are added back. The result happens to be correct, but probably by accident.
- **Previous owner with no share:** if `fromUser` has no share entry, they end up with a share of `0` (no rights) instead of nothing.
- **Test gap:** no test checks the README promise that the previous owner keeps their other rights. One that checks `ana` still has `READ | COMMENT | WRITE` would cover it.

**🟢 These look fine**
- `toggleRight` uses `^`, which matches what the README says the switches do. I'd add a test that a switch also turns a right *off*, since only turning on is tested now.
- `canComment` correctly checks COMMENT and blocks it when the document is locked.
- The CHANGELOG entry, version bump to 3.2.0 and README sections all match the code.
